key_insight: Gemini had the highest observed accuracy (90.29%), but SVM and the best transformer were not statistically distinguishable in this Bangla specialty-classification study.
clinical_relevance: Classifying informal Bangla patient narratives could support referral workflows, but this study does not establish clinical safety or improved patient outcomes.
method: Retained 2,730 patient records across the five most represented medical specialties.
Compared six ML models, four deep learning models, four fine-tuned transformers, and five zero-shot LLMs using a shared 80:20 train–test split.
Evaluated accuracy and macro-F1, with Holm-corrected paired McNemar tests for model comparisons.
evidence_signal: Leading accuracy/macro-F1 scores were Gemini 90.29%/90.15%, XLM-RoBERTa 86.26%/86.21%, SVM 84.98%/84.92%, and Bidirectional GRU 80.77%/80.83%.
watch_item: Restricting evaluation to five of the original 20 specialties limits generalizability to broader referral settings.
paper_title: Medical Specialty Prediction from Bangla Patient Narratives: A Comparative Study of ML, DL, Transformers, and LLMs
